name: Disorder of Purine Metabolism

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Purine Metabolism Disorders

criteria.description: Demonstration of deficiency or abnormal activity of purine metabolism enzymes (e.g., HGPRT deficiency)
Elevated serum and/or urinary uric acid levels
Presence of characteristic clinical features such as gout, nephrolithiasis, or neurological symptoms
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes involved in purine metabolism

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of enzyme deficiency or abnormal activity plus elevated uric acid levels and characteristic clinical features
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing can confirm diagnosis but is not mandatory if biochemical and clinical criteria are met.

pathognomonic.notes: Leads to gouty arthritis and tophi formation
searchTerms: high uric acid causing joint crystals

pathognomonic.symptomName: Neurological dysfunction due to HGPRT deficiency
pathognomonic.notes: Includes dystonia, choreoathetosis, and cognitive impairment
searchTerms: neurological problems from HGPRT enzyme deficiency
brain dysfunction due to metabolic defect
movement and cognitive issues from enzyme loss

common.notes: Due to uric acid crystal precipitation

searchTerms: hard nodules under skin from urate deposits

occasional.symptomName: Renal impairment due to urate nephropathy
occasional.notes: May progress to chronic kidney disease
searchTerms: renal impairment due to urate buildup

occasional.notes: Due to chronic disease or renal involvement

rare.symptomName: Cardiovascular complications secondary to chronic kidney disease
rare.notes: Rare but possible in advanced disease
searchTerms: heart and blood vessel problems from kidney disease
heart complications linked to kidney failure

laboratory: Elevated serum and urinary uric acid
Reduced HGPRT enzyme activity in erythrocytes or fibroblasts
imaging: Joint X-rays showing erosions and tophi
genetic: Pathogenic variants in HPRT1 gene or other purine metabolism genes
other: Detection of urate crystals in synovial fluid

redFlags: Early onset neurological dysfunction with hyperuricemia
references: Lesch-Nyhan syndrome and related disorders of purine metabolism: clinical and molecular aspects. N Engl J Med. 2000.
